Panama has introduced a 12-month Working Holiday visa for young foreigners

Panama has created a new visa in the non-resident category that allows young foreigners to stay in the country for up to 12 months and work temporarily under the "Vacaciones y Trabajo" program (Working Holiday). The corresponding Executive Decree No. 21 of October 13, 2026, was published in the Official Gazette on October 14 and came into effect on the same day.

The visa is only available to citizens of countries with which Panama has bilateral agreements under this program. Applicants must be between 18 and 30 years old at the time of application. The duration of stay is up to 12 months without the possibility of extension. After the program ends, the foreigner must leave the country.

Separate permission from the Ministry of Labor and Labor Development (Mitradel) is required to engage in paid work. The decree explicitly prohibits engaging in permanent work activities and applying for residency during the visa's validity period. Changing immigration categories is also not allowed.

Documents required include a notarized copy of the passport, three photographs, an apostilled birth certificate and a police clearance certificate from the country of origin, a certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirming participation in the program, medical insurance for the entire stay, and proof of sufficient funds to sustain oneself in Panama.

The new visa differs from the Remote Workers visa introduced in 2021, which is meant for those who solely earn income from abroad and do not work in the Panamanian labor market.

📌 Order Book Spoofing: When a Large Order Becomes a Trap

Main Points
⏺ A large order in the book doesn't always reflect genuine buying or selling interest
⏺ Some participants place orders to create a false impression of supply or demand
⏺ This post explains how to recognize suspicious activity and avoid market manipulation

1️⃣ Core Idea — spoofing happens when a trader places large orders without intending to execute them, attempting to influence other market participants.
2️⃣ How It Works — a large buy wall appears in the order book, suggesting strong support. Other traders begin buying, but the wall suddenly disappears.
3️⃣ Risk Surface — beginners may treat a large order as confirmation of market direction and enter positions based on a misleading signal.
4️⃣ What Matters — cancelling a large order alone doesn't prove manipulation. Repeated patterns and intent are important.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — analyze executed trades, volume, and liquidity changes instead of trusting impressive numbers in the order book.

Final Thoughts

An order book displays intentions, not guaranteed executions. Sometimes the biggest order exists only to make other traders react.

Pi Network’s official node documentation confirms that Mainnet operators must upgrade their software to Protocol 28, with the rollout scheduled for October 16. The October 13 deadline for node operators comes as the network continues developing smart contract capabilities and exploring stablecoin applications. 

🌐 Despite the approaching upgrade, PI has remained under selling pressure, trading at approximately $0.08042, down 7.32% over the past week. The upcoming Protocol 28 rollout is the latest stage of Pi Network’s 2026 blockchain development schedule. The project began the year with Protocol 19.6 in February, followed by versions 19.9 and 20.2 in March. Subsequent updates introduced technical improvements designed to support more advanced applications and smart contracts.

✨ Earlier in the year, Pi Network confirmed that Protocol 20 established the technical foundation for smart contracts, including applications involving subscriptions, escrow and digital assets. The team said these functions would undergo development, community review and testing before becoming available on Mainnet. The next planned release, Protocol 28, has attracted attention from Pi community members. X user Giannis Andreou stated that the upgrade was operating on Testnet, with Mainnet activation expected on October 16. 📣 Cardano’s Hoskinson challenges Vitalik over AI threats to crypto 

⚠️ Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson has challenged Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin over his warning that advances in artificial intelligence could weaken quantum-resistant cryptography, arguing that existing security standards already account for decades of mathematical attacks. Hoskinson responded on October 9 to Buterin’s concerns about lattice-based cryptography, which is used in several modern security systems. He argued that the Ethereum founder had not identified a credible new attack that would justify abandoning those methods or substantially increasing cryptographic key sizes. The disagreement follows Buterin’s warning that AI could uncover mathematical shortcuts that researchers have not discovered through conventional methods. 

🔔 He identified lattice-based cryptography as a particular concern, arguing that increasingly capable AI systems might discover more efficient ways to solve mathematical problems used to protect digital information. In his view, advances in automated mathematical research could compress decades of discoveries into a much shorter period. Such progress could force developers to reconsider the security of existing algorithms.

📊 Buterin compared the possible development to advances in integer factorization, where researchers discovered methods that made certain calculations much easier than earlier estimates suggested. The Ethereum co-founder argued that lattice-based security could experience a similar breakthrough, making some current parameter choices insufficient.
